statement.p: Find the Jacobian. \frac{\partial (x,y,z)}{\partial (s,t,u)}, where x = 5t-s+5u, y = 5s+t-5u, z = 4s+5t-2u.

static.solution: \left|\frac{\partial (x,y,z)}{\partial (s,t,u)}\right| = \left|\begin{array}{ccc} x_s \amp x_t \amp x_u\\ y_s \amp y_t \amp y_u\\ z_s \amp z_t \amp z_u \end{array}\right| =\left|\begin{array}{ccc} -1 \amp 5 \amp 5\\ 5 \amp 1 \amp -5\\ 4 \amp 5 \amp -2 \end{array}\right|. This 3 \times 3 determinant is computed the same way as for the cross product, with the entries -1,5,5 in the first row playing the same role as \vec i,\vec j,\vec k. We get \frac{\partial (x,y,z)}{\partial (s,t,u)}= ((1)(-2)-(-5)(5))-1 + ((-5)(4)-(5)(-2))5 + ((5)(5)-(1)(4))5 = 32.
